newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Citibank arranges $175mln loan for Czech Eurotel.
newsitem.headline: Citibank arranges $175mln loan for Czech Eurotel.

text.p: Citibank a.s. said on Thursday it had successfully syndicated a $175 million revolving crediit facility for Czech mobile phone operator Eurotel s.r.o., increasing a previous loan facility by $110 million.
"Citibank arranged a US$65 million facility for EuroTel in April 1996, which has now been increased by US$110 million and extended by six months until October 1st 1997," Citibank Prague said.
"Despite a very short syndication period, the offer was oversubscribed about 1.7 times," it said.
Neither Citibank nor Eurotel disclosed the loan's interest rate.
Eurotel spokeswoman Iva Tatounova said the mobile phone operator would use the additional funds to expand its new global system for mobile (GSM) network which it launched in early autumn.
"The obtained funds will be used to finance and expand the advanced digital GSM network and to purchase new technologies and mobile telephones for customers," Eurotel said.

Eurotel is locked in fierce competition with the Czech Republic's other mobile phone service Paegas, which is owned by Radiomobil a.s, a consortium led by Germany's DeTeMobil and Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s.
Before GSM, Eurotel was the monopoly provider of an analogue mobile phone system which it now runs concurrently with the new system.

Citibank named the other banks participating in the deal as: ABN Amro, Bank of America, ING Bank, Deutsche Bank, Sumitomo Bank, BNP Dresdner, Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka, Chase Manhattan, Commerzbank, Creditanstalt, Credit Suisse, Dai-Ichi Kangyo, Fuji Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, Sanwa Bank and Westdeutsche Lanbdesbank.
